correctness.rationale: Circular two-arc support lemma uses q>=3 and one circular run per letter. Removing complete periods reduces any Abelian square to two adjacent residue arcs; complement arcs handle residue>p/2. Different start phases give distinct factors whenever length>=p. Counting run placements yields F_h and the coefficient p+2 sum floor(r_i^2/4); exact k=1,2,3 boundary analysis and k-to-k+2 phase-preserving shift prove every k. A reproducible literal verifier checks 997 cases, 14021 length profiles and 4340 cyclic-arc instances without treating finite checks as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete all-length, all-run-length spectrum and exact period-two increment concern distinct Abelian-square *factors*, a useful invariant for Abelian-square reporting on compressed periodic words. The parity/boundary correction detects information absent from Abelian factor-Parikh complexity and sharply distinguishes alphabet sizes q>=3 versus q=2. The class is infinite and natural; the result is not a one-off computation, trivial reparametrization, or generic upper bound.
